report:
## Conclusion: The claim is accurate

The evidence strongly supports the claim that Kyleena (levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system, 19.5 mg) is FDA-approved for pregnancy prevention for up to 5 years.

**Regulatory evidence:** The FDA approved Kyleena in September 2016. Bayer's official press release confirms: "FDA Approves Bayer's Kyleena™ (Levonorgestrel-Releasing Intrauterine System) 19.5 mg for Prevention of Pregnancy for up to Five Years" (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/fda-approves-bayers-kyleena-levonorgestrel-releasing-intrauterine-system-195-mg-for-prevention-of-pregnancy-for-up-to-five-years-300330006.html). The official FDA-approved prescribing information states directly: "Kyleena is indicated to prevent pregnancy for up to 5 years" and instructs that it "should not remain in the uterus after 5 years," with replacement recommended if continued use is desired (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/208224s000lbl.pdf).

**Clinical trial basis:** This approval was supported by FDA review of Phase III clinical trial data using the Pearl Index—the standard contraceptive efficacy endpoint—which tracked pregnancies during use and shortly after removal/expulsion across the study period, as documented in the FDA's own summary review (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208224Orig1s000SumR.pdf).

**Corroborating clinical sources:** Independent medical and health information sites (Drugs.com, WebMD, Medical News Today) consistently reaffirm the 5-year approved duration, noting Kyleena can be replaced every 5 years if continued contraception is desired.

**Bottom line:** This claim is well-supported by primary regulatory documentation (FDA label and NDA approval records) and corroborated by clinical trial data and secondary medical sources. The 5-year approval reflects both the device's hormone-release mechanism and clinical efficacy data submitted to and accepted by the FDA.
